open_points.subject: owner session cookie
open_points.text: “carried by a cookie that scripts cannot read, sent only over HTTPS when the interface is reached from another machine, and only to Registry's own origin”
open_points.question: What exact cookie scope and transport rules apply, especially on same-host HTTP and across hosts, ports, paths and cross-site requests?
options: Require HttpOnly, host-only, a fixed Path, SameSite, and Secure on every deployment
Allow a non-Secure cookie on same-host HTTP while defining the remaining scope attributes
Treat “own origin” as host-only even though browser cookies are not port-bound
open_points.default_guess: Use an HttpOnly, host-only, SameSite=Strict cookie with Path=/ and Secure whenever HTTPS is used.

open_points.subject: concurrent owner-session requests
open_points.text: “applied one at a time, in the order they reach the session”
open_points.question: How is the order determined when concurrent requests reach different workers or have no observable total arrival order?
options: Order by acquisition of a per-session lock
Assign a monotonic arrival sequence before dispatch
Allow either order and specify both outcomes as valid
open_points.default_guess: Use acquisition order of a per-session lock and permit either winner for simultaneous arrivals.

open_points.subject: owner session and confirmation value generation
open_points.text: “each at least 32 bytes from the operating system's random source”
open_points.question: What happens if a newly generated session identity, CSRF value or confirmation value equals a live or previously relevant value?
options: Regenerate until unique in the applicable scope
Accept the negligible collision risk
Refuse the request that attempted to create it
open_points.default_guess: Regenerate session identities until globally unique among live sessions and regenerate CSRF or confirmation values until distinct within that session.

open_points.subject: confirmation input binding
open_points.text: “kept as a digest of those values in a fixed order”
open_points.question: What exact canonical encoding, digest algorithm and treatment of absent, blank, ordered and structured values define equality with the confirmed inputs?
options: Define a typed canonical serialization and a cryptographic digest
Digest the eventual wire encoding
Store and compare the normalized values instead of only a digest
open_points.default_guess: Use a versioned, typed canonical serialization with explicit absence markers and a collision-resistant cryptographic digest.

open_points.subject: confirmation-step display
open_points.text: “Every operation — read or change ... checks in one order” and “made when a confirmation step is shown”
open_points.question: Which A04 checks must pass before Registry shows a confirmation step and installs its pending confirmation: only session and CSRF checks, or also existence, values, revision and lifecycle checks for the proposed action?
options: Run all applicable checks except the final transition before showing the step
Check only owner session and CSRF when showing it
Use a separate declared check sequence for confirmation previews
open_points.default_guess: Run all non-mutating checks, including current revision and lifecycle, before showing the confirmation step, then repeat them on submission.

open_points.subject: import mapping contents
open_points.text: “the mapping shows for the picks only: their rooms and pointers; the display name and alias each will arrive under”
open_points.question: Does the mapping show every imported fact of the picked projects—especially the embedded object, references, statuses and retained instants—or only the items expressly named?
options: Show every fact that the transaction will store
Show only the named summary while validating hidden facts
Show all personal and identity facts but summarize retained history
open_points.default_guess: Show every fact that will be stored, grouped under each picked project.

open_points.subject: empty import selection
open_points.text: “the owner picks any subset of its projects” and “an accepted import stores every picked project”
open_points.question: May the owner confirm an empty set, and if so does that empty import create the migration closure and permanently close importing?
options: Refuse confirmation unless at least one project is picked
Accept an empty import and close the migration
Accept it without creating the closure
open_points.default_guess: Refuse confirmation when no project is picked.

open_points.subject: replacement after an upload-time refusal
open_points.text: “a refused upload — too large or unreadable — replaces nothing” and “a file ... that holds two project records with one id ... is refused whole at upload”
open_points.question: Do all upload-time refusals preserve the session's previously uploaded file, or only the specifically named too-large and unreadable cases?
options: Every refused upload preserves the previous file and confirmation state
Only size and decoding failures preserve it; structural failures replace or clear it
Every upload attempt clears the previous file before validation
open_points.default_guess: Every refused upload preserves the previous uploaded file and its pending state.

open_points.subject: import file digest
open_points.text: “The mapping names the file by its digest”
open_points.question: Which digest algorithm and byte representation identify the uploaded file, and what must Registry do if two different byte sequences produce the same digest?
options: Use a specified collision-resistant digest of the original bytes and refuse a detected collision
Digest a canonical parsed representation
Treat digest equality as file identity without collision handling
open_points.default_guess: Use SHA-256 over the exact uploaded bytes and additionally require the currently held bytes to be the same file bound to the confirmation.

open_points.subject: configuration item validation
open_points.question: What makes each configuration item well formed beyond the separately stated secret length and path checks?
options: Define a grammar and representation for every item
Treat any nonempty value of the expected runtime type as well formed
Leave parsing rules to the implementation
open_points.default_guess: Define an explicit representation and parser for every configuration item, rejecting invalid encoding and empty path values.

open_points.subject: unknown configuration items
open_points.text: “every item of rule 1 present and none unknown”
open_points.question: Which names are considered Registry configuration for the unknown-item check, rather than unrelated environment or process settings?
options: Check only entries in a dedicated Registry namespace
Require the entire supplied environment/configuration object to contain only the listed names
Ignore all unknown entries
open_points.default_guess: Use a dedicated Registry configuration namespace and reject unknown names only inside it.

open_points.subject: backup retention bound
open_points.text: “deletes every kept backup made more than 30 × 24 hours before” and “an erasure reaches the backups at most 30 days after it”
open_points.question: At the exact 30-day boundary, is a backup deleted or retained until the next daily run, which can keep erased data for almost 31 days?
options: Delete backups whose age is at least 30 × 24 hours
Keep the strict ‘more than’ rule and change the stated erasure bound to almost 31 days
Run an additional deletion when each backup reaches exactly 30 days
open_points.default_guess: Delete a backup when its age is at least 30 × 24 hours.

open_points.subject: overlapping scheduled backup runs
open_points.question: If a run is still active at the next 03:00 UTC, is that day's run skipped, queued to start after the active run, or does the active run fail?
options: Skip the new occurrence with no catch-up
Queue exactly one run to start afterward
Cancel or fail one of the runs
open_points.default_guess: Skip the new occurrence and record a diagnostic.

open_points.subject: 03:00 startup boundary
open_points.text: “Every day at 03:00 UTC, while Registry runs ... it makes one backup run”
open_points.question: If Registry starts or finishes configuration checks at exactly 03:00 UTC, what determines whether that day's run occurs?
options: Run if serving begins no later than the scheduler's 03:00 event
Treat a start at 03:00 as missed and wait until the next day
Run once whenever startup occurs during a defined 03:00 window
open_points.default_guess: Run only if the scheduler observes Registry already serving at the 03:00 event.

open_points.subject: newest-backup owner view
open_points.text: “The owner interface shows the instant of the newest kept backup”
open_points.question: What does the owner interface show when no kept backup exists, including before the first successful run or after cleanup removes every kept file?
options: Show an explicit ‘no kept backup’ state
Omit the value
Refuse the view as unavailable

open_points.subject: backup cleanup failure
open_points.text: “it deletes every kept backup ... and every file under the kept prefix that cannot be read as a backup” and “A step that fails ... writes a diagnostic”
open_points.question: If deleting one kept file fails, does Registry stop cleanup immediately or continue attempting the remaining deletions, and how is the run classified?
options: Stop at the first deletion failure
Continue all deletions and report every failure
Continue all deletions but report one failed run
open_points.default_guess: Continue attempting all independent deletions, then mark the run failed and report the failed paths without sensitive values.

open_points.subject: backup metadata integrity
open_points.text: “It records, readable without its key, its instant, the release that made it, the last audit sequence number it holds and a digest of the key”
open_points.question: Is the readable metadata authenticated by the encrypted backup, and what happens when metadata is altered but the encrypted store still decrypts and passes its own integrity check?
options: Authenticate all metadata and reject any mismatch
Leave metadata unauthenticated and validate only the stated cross-checks
Store a second authenticated copy inside the encrypted payload and require equality
open_points.default_guess: Authenticate the metadata and require it to equal a copy inside the encrypted payload.

open_points.subject: backup of a store with no audit entries
open_points.text: “records ... the last audit sequence number it holds” and “checks ... that its audit log ends at the recorded sequence number”
open_points.question: What value is recorded and what check is performed when the store has never written an audit entry?
options: Record sequence 0 and require an empty log with counter 0
Record no value and require an empty log
Refuse to make a backup until an audit entry exists
open_points.default_guess: Record 0 and require both an empty audit log and a stored next-sequence state consistent with 0.

open_points.subject: pending confirmation model for unversioned actions
open_points.text: “at most one pending confirmation — its one-time value, the action, its target, the revision or access version ...”
open_points.question: What revision-or-access-version fact does the OwnerSession carry for confirmed actions that have neither, particularly the import and erasure of old audit entries?
options: Make the bound revision/access version optional when the action has none
Use a distinct action-specific concurrency value
Do not allow pending confirmations for unversioned actions
open_points.default_guess: Make the version binding absent for actions with no revision or access version.
